title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties. .Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused river levels on the St Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. The river may hold steady early this week with continued rises through Major Flood Stage then forecast mid to late week. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Campground are inaccessible due to knee-deep water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 4.1 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 8:30 AM EST Sunday was 4.1 feet. - Forecast...The river is forecast to hold steady near 4.1 feet early this week with continued rises through Major Flood Stage forecast mid to late week. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of record. * WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney. * WHEN...Until further notice. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 12.8 feet. - Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 AM EST Sunday was 12.8 feet. - Forecast...River levels are forecast to reach a crest of 13.1 feet tonight, before beginning a very slow decline within Major flood stage later in the week. - Flood stage is 8.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
